# Results — Study 537 (Factor-Momentum) on a real yfinance survivor panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: build a monthly
long-short factor panel (momentum, low-vol, low-beta, short-reversal, size-proxy) from a fixed
large-cap survivor basket, run **time-series momentum on the factors** (hold a factor long when
its trailing return is positive, short when negative), and test the timed meta-premium against
zero with a one-sample/HAC t and a time-shuffle placebo. One-month execution lag at the factor
level; one-way costs × turnover + borrow on short sleeves. Data pulled **2026-06-26**; the
partial in-progress month (June 2026) is **excluded** — the panel ends on the last complete
month, **2026-05-29** (no partial periods in a stamped run). As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 5656 days × 40 names + SPY | `f3d05a8825d4` |
| Factor panel (monthly long-short) | 262 months × 5 factors | `176062fe6aaf` |
| Period covered | 2004-08-31 — 2026-05-29 (21.7 years) | — |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (`auto_adjust=True`). Five **price-derived**
long-short factors, top-third minus bottom-third, rebalanced monthly: `mom` (12-1 momentum),
`lowvol` (low trailing-vol), `lowbeta` (low rolling-beta vs SPY), `strev` (1-month reversal),
`size` (a price-only liquidity/quietness proxy — *named a proxy*, not a market-cap factor).

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is 40 large-caps still trading in 2026.
Failed firms — natural members of the factors' short legs — are absent, tilting the long legs
up. All results are **upper-bound estimates**.

**Fundamental-data limitation (named explicitly):** a genuine *value* or *quality* factor needs
point-in-time fundamentals. yfinance `.info` (P/B, P/E) is a single current snapshot — not
point-in-time and flaky on CI — so we do **not** fabricate a value factor from it. The panel is
deliberately price-only; the meta-premium is tested on the factors we *can* build honestly.

## Are the factors themselves persistent? (the Ehsani-Linnainmaa premise)

| Factor | Static mean | lag-1 autocorr |
|---|--:|--:|
| `mom` | -1.44%/yr | +0.151 |
| `lowvol` | -5.22%/yr | +0.177 |
| `lowbeta` | -4.87%/yr | +0.152 |
| `strev` | +0.15%/yr | -0.130 |
| `size` | -5.14%/yr | +0.157 |

Four of five factors show **positive month-to-month autocorrelation** (~0.15) — the premise of
factor-momentum holds: factors that did well recently tend to keep doing well. (Note the static
means are mostly **negative** on this survivor large-cap tape — the 2010s megacap decade punished
low-vol / low-beta / size — so the question is whether *timing* the factors rescues that.)

## The honest test — time-series-momentum-timed meta-premium

For each factor, position = sign(trailing-return through t-1); timed return = position ×
factor_return[t]; the factor-momentum series = the mean across factors.

| Lookback | Mean | Vol | Sharpe | one-sample t | HAC t | Hit | Max DD | placebo p |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | +1.01%/yr | 13.0% | 0.08 | +0.36 | +0.45 | 53% | -32.4% | 0.267 |
| 3m | **+2.10%/yr** | 13.1% | 0.16 | **+0.75** | +1.06 | 52% | -29.7% | **0.096** |
| 6m | +1.36%/yr | 12.2% | 0.11 | +0.51 | +0.56 | 54% | -47.6% | 0.199 |
| 12m | +0.49%/yr | 13.5% | 0.04 | +0.16 | +0.18 | 52% | -55.5% | 0.413 |

- The best configuration (3-month lookback) earns **+2.10%/yr** at one-sample **t = +0.75**
  (HAC t = +1.06) — **well below** the desk's |t| ≥ 2 bar. The time-shuffle placebo
  **p = 0.096** (seed-robust over 20 seeds: mean 0.102, range 0.085–0.116) does not clear 0.05
  either. The meta-premium is **not** statistically distinguishable from zero on this panel.
- **Timing does beat holding the factors static:** the static (untimed) average factor *loses*
  **-3.36%/yr** (t = -1.18); timing turns that into a small **positive** (+2.10%/yr). The
  *direction* matches Ehsani-Linnainmaa — timing adds value — but the magnitude is thin and the
  significance is absent.

## Costs × turnover

| Lookback | Gross | Net | Turnover | Short frac | net t |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | +1.03%/yr | -0.38%/yr | 0.96 | 0.51 | -0.14 |
| 3m | +2.08%/yr | **+1.16%/yr** | 0.55 | 0.53 | +0.41 |
| 6m | +1.29%/yr | +0.59%/yr | 0.36 | 0.54 | +0.22 |
| 12m | +0.47%/yr | -0.15%/yr | 0.29 | 0.56 | -0.05 |

10 bps one-way × per-sleeve turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow on short sleeves. The 1-month and
12-month lookbacks go **net-negative**; even the best 3-month config nets only **+1.16%/yr** at
net t = 0.41. The shorter the lookback, the more a factor's sign flips and the heavier the
turnover bill (0.96 vs 0.29 monthly). Operationally this is a **Mirage**.

## Per-factor timed contribution (3-month lookback)

| Factor | Timed mean | t |
|---|--:|--:|
| `mom` | +0.10%/yr | +0.03 |
| `lowvol` | +5.84%/yr | +1.43 |
| `lowbeta` | +1.66%/yr | +0.40 |
| `strev` | -2.30%/yr | -0.79 |
| `size` | +5.06%/yr | +1.19 |

What positive premium there is comes from timing `lowvol` and `size`; timing `strev`
(short-reversal) actively *hurts*. No single sleeve clears t = 2.

## Robustness — long-only-on-negative

Holding a factor **flat** (instead of short) when its trailing return is negative removes the
premium entirely: 3-month **-0.52%/yr** (t = -0.26), 12-month **-1.17%/yr** (t = -0.47). The
modest gross premium depends on the (costly, hard-to-borrow) short leg.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

| Planted AR(1) | Timed mean | t | placebo p |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (white noise) | +1.59%/yr | +1.19 | 0.115 |
| 0.30 (real persistence) | +10.70%/yr | +7.88 | 0.000 |

With **no** planted persistence the timing does **not** clear t = 2 and the placebo stays at
p ≈ 0.12 (no false positive — the small positive bias from overlapping windows is exactly what
the placebo absorbs). With a **+0.30** planted AR(1) the meta-premium lights up (t = 7.88,
p = 0.000). The detector recovers genuine factor persistence and refuses to manufacture it from
noise — so the real-tape t ≈ 0.75 is an honest read, not an engine artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The factors *are* persistent (autocorr ~0.15, four of five positive) and
  timing them beats holding them static (turns -3.36%/yr into +2.10%/yr) — the Ehsani-Linnainmaa
  *direction* is there. But the meta-premium is **+2.10%/yr at t = +0.75**, placebo **p = 0.096**
  — it does **not** clear the |t| ≥ 2 + placebo bar on this 22-year, 5-factor survivor panel.
  WEAK rather than NONE only because the premise (factor persistence) and the direction
  (timing > static) survive; the tradable premium does not.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of costs the best config nets +1.16%/yr (net t = 0.41); short
  and long lookbacks go net-negative. Sharpe ≤ 0.15, drawdowns -30% to -55%, and the premium
  leans on a costly short leg (long-only-on-negative kills it). Not investable.
- **Do the factors trend? — CONFIRMED.** The study's distinct axis: month-to-month factor
  autocorrelation is positive and consistent (~0.15 across mom/lowvol/lowbeta/size). The
  *premise* of factor-momentum holds even where the *tradable* meta-premium, on a thin
  large-cap survivor basket with real costs, does not.
